scope.description: Two probes on freshly built single-voter clusters whose node 1 is made leader with everything committed applied. Each probe proposes a ConfChangeV2 through the real MsgProp path, checks that the entry committed, then applies it through the documented application path with the panic recovered, and records the voters before and after.
assumptions: The leader is made to win directly (becomeCandidate + becomeLeader) so the single-voter cluster is ready without a network round trip.
Proposals are stepped as pb.Message{Type: MsgProp, Entries: [{Type: EntryConfChangeV2, Data: marshalled ConfChangeV2}]}, which is the shape Node.ProposeConfChange delivers.
In a single-voter cluster the leader's own acknowledgment is the quorum, so the entry commits once it is appended and its self-acknowledgment is processed.
The application path for a committed conf-change entry is ApplyConfChange, which the harness calls with the same ConfChangeV2 and recovers any panic verbatim.
No restart, snapshot, joint configuration or peer traffic is involved.
excluded: The embedding application's own validation or operator interfaces
Process-level effects of the recovered panic and any restart behaviour

basis.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). Each probe builds a real raft instance with newTestRaft(1, 10, 1, newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(voters...))), calls becomeCandidate and becomeLeader so the single-voter cluster is ready, advances the applied index and clears the queues. It emits conf_change_setup with probe_id, scenario, voters_before, pendingConfIndex, applied, committed, node state and term; marshals the ConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp into the leader and records the returned error; takes the appended index, processes the leader's own acknowledgment through readMessages so the entry commits (the self-ack of a single-voter leader is the quorum), and records whether the committed index covers the proposed index. It then calls applyConfChange with the same ConfChangeV2 inside a recover, recording panicked, the verbatim recovered value, the voters afterwards and the node state, and emits conf_change_apply. Probes: 'remove-last-voter' (ConfChangeV2 removing node 1 from a {1} cluster) and 'add-voter-control' (ConfChangeV2 adding node 2 to a {1} cluster), which must not abort. The test asserts that both proposals committed so that a failure to commit cannot be mistaken for the measured outcome.
basis.responsibility: The proposal and apply paths own keeping the configuration serviceable: a change whose application cannot produce a usable configuration must be rejected before it is committed or reported to the application, not converted into an abort of the node that applies it.

comparisons.description: Applying a committed conf change that removes the last voter does not abort the applying node.
Control: applying a committed add-voter change of the same shape does not abort the applying node.
